Life cycle greenhouse gas emissions of U.S. beef production are highly variable and dependent on assumptions made about emissions from enteric fermentation and manure management, and the inclusion of emissions from indirect land-use change and soil management.

the main sources of variability in life cycle GHG estimates for U.S. beef production are: (1) uncertainty in emissions from indirect land change, pasture soil carbon sequestrations, methane from feedlot manures, and enteric fermentation from pasture, (2) variability in feedlot emissions, and (3) variability in the feedlot to slaughter ratio.
life cycle GHG estimates from U.S. feedlot beef production are sensitive to uncertainty associated with indirect land use change (iLUC) and enteric fermentation (EF).
